data.name: Lucaniel
data.gender_notes: Lucaniel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman family name 'Lucanus', meaning 'from Lucania'. In Christianity, it is also the name of a 4th-century Christian martyr. Lucaniel may symbolize a beacon of light in one's life or spiritual journey. The name Lucaniel carries the meaning “Bright light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lucaniel usually hope their child will grow to embody bright light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of enlightenment and guidance.
data.etymology: Lucaniel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bright light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lucaniel total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: לוקניאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לוקניאל הוא שם המשלב את השורשים העבריים לוק (אור) וניאל (אלוהים הוא שופטי) או נאל (הוא שופט אותנו), ומשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא המאיר והמשפיע עלי' או 'אלוהים הוא שופטי האור'. השם מורכב מל'וק', שפירושו אור, ומ'ניאל', שפירושו אלוהים הוא שופטי. השם לוקניאל משדר תחושה של הארה אלוהית ומשפט צדק.

in_greek.name: Λουκανιέλ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι το φως και η κρίση μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λουκανιέλ προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές ρίζες 'Λουκ' (φως) και 'νιέλ' (Θεός είναι η κρίση μου). Η λέξη 'Λουκ' σχετίζεται με το φως, ενώ 'νιέλ' σημαίνει ότι ο Θεός είναι ο κριτής μου. Ο συνδυασμός τους δίνει το νόημα 'Ο Θεός είναι το φως και η κρίση μου' ή 'Ο Θεός είναι αυτός που φωτίζει και κρίνει'. Το όνομα αυτό έχει έντονη πνευματική διάσταση και συνδέεται με την έννοια της θείας καθοδήγησης και κρίσης.

in_latin.name: Lucaniel
in_latin.meaning: Deus est lux et iudicium meum
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lucaniel ex radicibus Latinis 'luc' (lux) et 'aniel' (Deus est iudicium) componitur. Significatio nominis est 'Deus est lux et iudicium meum' vel 'Deus est qui illuminat et iudicat'. Nomen hoc profundam spiritualem habet significationem et coniungitur cum conceptu divine ductus et iudicii. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc potest significare illuminationem et protectionem divinam.

in_english.name: Lucaniel
in_english.meaning: God is my light and judgment
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lucaniel is derived from the Hebrew roots 'Luk' (light) and 'Niel' (God is my judge). It carries the meaning 'God is my light and judgment' or 'God is the one who illuminates and judges'. This name has a strong spiritual connotation, symbolizing divine guidance, illumination, and justice. In Christian tradition, Lucaniel may signify a person's reliance on God's wisdom and protection. The name combines the essence of light and divine judgment, suggesting a person who seeks guidance from God in all aspects of life.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lucaniel derives from the ancient Roman surname 'Lucanus', which means 'from Lucania' - an ancient region in southern Italy. This cultural background adds a rich historical depth to the name, connecting it to the ancient Roman civilization.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Lucaniel also holds spiritual significance in Christianity. It echoes the name of Saint Lucan, a 4th-century Italian bishop venerated for his devotion and steadfastness in the face of persecution. Lucaniel may be seen as a reminder to shine a light in the darkest corners of one's life, remaining steadfast and committed to their spiritual path.

historical_references.reference: Saint Lucaniel, also known as Lucan, was a bishop of Beauvais in the 6th century. He is said to have been a disciple of St. Remigius, the first bishop of Reims. According to legend, Lucaniel was sent by St. Remigius to evangelize the pagan tribes of Picardy. He was martyred around 541 AD after refusing to renounce his faith during a pagan festival. His relics are now enshrined in the abbey of Saint-Riquier in the Somme valley.
historical_references.context: Early Christian era, missionary work, martyrdom

In 1429, Lucaniel was captured by English forces and taken to England, where he was held prisoner for several years. During this time, he became friends with King Henry VI of England and served as a advisor and confidant. Lucaniel was eventually released and returned to France, where he continued to serve his king, Charles VII.
